title: Sensitivity labels: what they classify, protect and tell Copilot to leave alone
summary: The controls, licensing statements and documented limits are supported by Microsoft's current documentation. Minor corrections should complete the Copilot DLP route, acknowledge conflicting guidance about changes to existing group labels, and add two supporting sources.

claims.claim: Labels are created in the Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create a label.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... On the Sensitivity labels page, select + Create a label

claims.claim: New-Label -Name <label name> -DisplayName <display name> -Tooltip <tooltip> creates a sensitivity label in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization. ... New-Label ... [-Name] <String> ... -DisplayName <String> ... -Tooltip <String>

claims.claim: Label publishing policies are created at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... On the Label policies page, select Publish label

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a sensitivity label policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management"

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive label support can be enabled at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables label support for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an admin UI for enabling sensitivity-label support for Microsoft 365 groups, teams and sites.
claims.quote: Searched: sensitivity labels EnableMIPLabels enable groups sites feature admin center UI PowerShell only. Read groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites; enablement uses PowerShell, while documented UI procedures assign labels after enablement.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId <setting id> -BodyParameter <params>, with EnableMIPLabels set to True, enables group label support.
claims.quote: Name = "EnableMIPLabels" ... Value = "True" ... Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policies are created at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy with Name, SharePointLocation, ApplySensitivityLabel and Mode TestWithoutNotifications creates the illustrated auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointLocation "<SharePointSiteLocation>" -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: The printed Copilot DLP route reaches the Copilot location in the Custom policy wizard.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: The route stops at the location selection rather than the label-based restriction. Extend the route in controls[5].ui and the matching rendered cell to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels'; retain the existing note naming the action 'Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content'.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -AdvancedRule <advanced rule> -RestrictAccess <settings> configures the Copilot restriction.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The modern label scheme uses + Create and then Label instead of + Create a label.
claims.quote: On the Sensitivity labels page, select + Create and then Label to start the new sensitivity label configuration.

claims.claim: Set-Label changes an existing label.
claims.quote: You can now use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure all the settings you see in your labeling admin center. ... Set-Label

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy changes a published label policy.
claims.quote: Additional label policy settings are available with the Set-LabelPolicy cmdlet from Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy exposes location parameters such as ExchangeLocation.
claims.quote: New-LabelPolicy ... [-ExchangeLocation <MultiValuedProperty>] ... [-ModernGroupLocation <MultiValuedProperty>] ... [-OneDriveLocation <MultiValuedProperty>]

claims.claim: Enabling SharePoint and OneDrive support through the portal requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: This option is the easiest way to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive. You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo requires PowerShell enablement in each geo-location.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable this support for all your geo-locations. ... Repeat steps 1 and 2 for each of your remaining geo-locations.

claims.claim: OneNote label support requires an additional Set-SPOTenant parameter.
claims.quote: If you want to additionally enable sensitivity labels for OneNote ... run Set-SPOTenant again ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableSensitivityLabelforOneNote $true

claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronizes sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID with the Execute-AzureAdLabelSync cmdlet in the Security & Compliance PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Configuring label support for Microsoft 365 groups requires at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.
claims.quote: To configure this feature, there must be at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling requires an E5 or P2-tier license or add-on.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels and manual labeling are — auto-labeling requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.claim: A Copilot-location DLP rule can identify labeled files and emails with Content contains > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels ... Detects when a file or an email in Exchange has a chosen sensitivity label.

claims.claim: The label rule's action is Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content

claims.claim: The PowerShell example uses RestrictAccess with ExcludeContentProcessing set to Block.
claims.quote: -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The example attaches the rule to a policy created with EnforcementPlanes CopilotExperiences.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels classify content using Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
claims.quote: With sensitivity labels, you can identify the sensitivity of data across your organization, and the label can enforce protection settings that are appropriate for the sensitivity of that data.

claims.claim: Labels are stored in file and email metadata.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in clear text in the metadata for files and emails, third-party apps and services can read it

claims.claim: A label stays with content wherever it is saved or stored.
claims.quote: Because the label is stored in metadata for files and emails, the label stays with the content, no matter where you save or store it.

claims.claim: Labels can encrypt files and emails and control who can access that content.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data.

claims.claim: Labels can enforce content markings.
claims.quote: Mark the content when you use Office apps, by adding watermarks, headers, or footers to email, meeting invites, or documents that have the label applied.

claims.claim: Container labels can control privacy for sites and groups.
claims.quote: These settings include privacy settings, external user access and external sharing, access from unmanaged devices, private teams discoverability, and sharing controls for channels.

claims.claim: Container labels can control sharing settings.
claims.quote: Protect containers ... For example, set privacy settings, external user access and external sharing, access from unmanaged devices, and control how channels can be shared with other teams.

claims.claim: Users can apply labels that administrators create and publish.
claims.quote: First, admins create and publish sensitivity labels to users and groups. Then, end users apply labels to emails and documents.

claims.claim: Office and other supporting apps and services enforce label protection settings.
claims.quote: Finally, Office or third-party apps/services enforce protection based on the applied labels.

claims.where: What it is: Parts of the mechanism, Scope
claims.claim: Label scope determines whether the label applies to files and other assets, emails, meetings, or groups and sites.
claims.quote: The scope determines two things: ... This scope configuration means you can have sensitivity labels that are just for items such as files, emails, and meetings, and can't be selected for groups and sites.

claims.where: What it is: Scope; Risks and limits: Container labels
claims.claim: A group or site label protects the container but does not label its documents or other items.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What it is: Priority; What to check
claims.claim: List order determines label priority, and Microsoft recommends putting the most restrictive label at the bottom.
claims.quote: The order of the labels is important because it sets their priority. You want your most restrictive sensitivity label, such as Highly Confidential, to appear at the bottom of the list

claims.claim: An item can carry one sensitivity label from the organization.
claims.quote: Each item that supports sensitivity labels can have a single sensitivity label applied to it from your organization.

claims.claim: A label policy can set a default label.
claims.quote: Specify a default label for unlabeled documents and Loop components and pages, emails and meeting invites, new containers

claims.claim: A label policy can require justification for lowering a label.
claims.quote: Require a justification for changing a label. For files, emails, and meetings ... if a user tries to remove a label or replace it with a label that has a lower priority

claims.claim: A label policy can require mandatory labeling.
claims.quote: Require users to apply a label for the different types of items and the containers that support sensitivity labels. Also known as mandatory labeling

claims.claim: Office client-side auto-labeling can apply or recommend a label.
claims.quote: This method supports recommending a label to users, as well as automatically applying a label.

claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling policies apply labels to SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content.
claims.quote: Service-side labeling when content is already saved (in SharePoint or OneDrive) or emailed (processed by Exchange Online): Use an auto-labeling policy.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Copilot agents recognize sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and agents have the capability to access data ... Just like your Office apps, Copilot and agents can access sensitivity labels from your organization

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Copilot Chat displays the highest-priority sensitivity label among the data used.
claims.quote: The latest response in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat ... display the highest priority sensitivity label from the data used for that Copilot chat.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels; Why it matters
claims.claim: When label encryption applies, Copilot and agents require the user's EXTRACT copy permission to return the data, subject to the stated Edge exception.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Without DLP in Edge, Copilot in Edge and Windows can reference encrypted content in the active Edge tab without EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Unless data loss prevention (DLP) is used in Edge, Copilot can reference encrypted content from the active browser tab in Edge when that content doesn't grant the user EXTRACT usage rights.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: New content created by Copilot in Word can inherit the source label.
claims.quote: If you use Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook to create new content based on an item that has a sensitivity label applied, the sensitivity label from the source file is automatically inherited

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: New content created by Copilot in PowerPoint can inherit the source label.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: New content created by Copilot in Outlook can inherit the source label.
claims.quote: Copilot in Word, Copilot in PowerPoint, and Copilot in Outlook support sensitivity label inheritance for newly created content.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: Label inheritance is unsupported for source encryption configured with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Label inheritance isn't supported when the encryption is configured for user-defined permissions or if the encryption was applied independently from the label.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels
claims.claim: In that unsupported inheritance case, the user cannot send the source data to the destination item.
claims.quote: The user won't be able to send this data to the destination item.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot and labels; Governance controls: reports
claims.claim: Retention is the separate mechanism for retaining or deleting content.
claims.quote: Although the main purpose of retention labels is to retain or delete content, you can also use retention labels without turning on any retention or other actions.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-reports to sources. These support the retention distinction and the Information Protection > Reports path respectively; the latter path is confirmed in the Reports page's Posture reports section. This is the grouped finding for supporting Microsoft pages not currently cited.

claims.claim: A Purview DLP policy can exclude labeled files and emails from Copilot and Cowork processing.
claims.quote: You can create a DLP policy to prevent these Copilot experiences from using files and emails that have sensitivity labels when generating responses.

claims.claim: eDiscovery search conditions can select content by sensitivity label.
claims.quote: The condition builder to create search queries in eDiscovery supports sensitivity labels that are applied to content.

claims.claim: The service description says Information Protection features are enabled at tenant level for all users by default.
claims.quote: By default, Information Protection features are enabled at the tenant level for all users within the tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 sensitivity-label capabilities use per-user subscriptions.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services

claims.claim: User licensing requirements depend on the sensitivity-label features used.
claims.quote: The licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The service-description table includes manual labeling in Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F1/F3 and Business Premium.
claims.quote: Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F1/F3/Business Premium ... Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Manual labelling; Open questions
claims.claim: The same introduction says labeling requires E5 or Information Protection and Governance, conflicting with the manual-labeling table.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E3 and Business Premium do not include auto-labeling of files and emails.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU.

claims.claim: Restricting Copilot processing of files and emails is included in the listed E5/A5, Purview Suite/EDU/FLW, Defender + Purview Suite FLW, IPG E5/A5/F5 and Office E5/A5 plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5 ... restrict Copilot from processing files and emails ... Included | Included

claims.claim: That file-and-email restriction is not included in the listed Business, Microsoft 365 E3-tier and Office 365 E3-tier plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Business Basic/Standard/Premium | Microsoft 365 E3/A3/A1/G3/F3/F1 | Office 365 E3/E1/A3/A1/G3/G1/F3 ... restrict Copilot from processing files and emails | Not included | Not included | Not included

claims.claim: Labeling non-Microsoft 365 Data Map assets and using protection policies require pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Specific to non-Microsoft 365 data sources, applying sensitivity labels in the Data Map and using protection policies requires you to set up pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: The cited documentation marks Data Map sensitivity-label extension as preview.
claims.quote: Extend sensitivity labels to assets in Microsoft Purview Data Map: When you turn on this capability, currently in preview

claims.claim: Protection policies for non-Microsoft 365 content are preview.
claims.quote: Protection policies are currently in preview and apply to items stored outside Microsoft 365.

claims.quote: Until you enable this feature, these services can't process encrypted files

claims.where: Risks and limits: Labels not enabled
claims.claim: Coauthoring does not work on those encrypted files before enablement.
claims.quote: Coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work for these files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Labels not enabled
claims.claim: eDiscovery does not work on those encrypted files before enablement.
claims.quote: Coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work for these files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Labels not enabled
claims.claim: DLP does not work on those encrypted files before enablement.
claims.quote: Coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work for these files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Labels not enabled
claims.claim: Search does not work on those encrypted files before enablement.
claims.quote: Coauthoring, eDiscovery, data loss prevention, search, and other collaborative features won't work for these files.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy automatically created from a label configuration runs in simulation when saved.
claims.quote: By default, all locations for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange are included in the auto-label policy, and when the policy is saved, it runs in simulation mode.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: That automatic policy creation does not check the prerequisite that SharePoint and OneDrive labels are enabled.
claims.quote: There's no check that you've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive, which is one of the prerequisites for auto-labeling to apply to content in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: Auto-labeling has a throughput ceiling of 500,000 files per day.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: The tenant limit is 100 auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: Explicit SharePoint site selection has a 1,000-site policy limit.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-labeling saved without a check
claims.claim: Simulation supports at most 20,000,000 matched files per policy simulation.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files. If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The overview says deleting a label does not automatically remove it from content.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label from the Microsoft Purview portal, the label isn't automatically removed from content

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The overview says protection continues to be enforced after deletion.
claims.quote: Any protection settings continue to be enforced on content that had that label applied.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The detailed deletion guide says container labels are removed.
claims.quote: For containers, such as sites in SharePoint and Teams: The label is removed

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The detailed deletion guide says container label settings stop being enforced.
claims.quote: Any settings that were configured with that label are no longer enforced.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The deletion guide documents encryption removal for processable documents in enabled SharePoint and OneDrive services.
claims.quote: If the deleted label applied encryption and the services can process the encrypted contents, the encryption is removed. Egress actions from these services result in the same outcome.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: Deleting an encrypting label archives its protection template.
claims.quote: If the label applied encryption, the underlying protection template is archived so that previously protected content can still be opened.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleting a label
claims.claim: The archived protection template prevents reuse of the deleted label's name.
claims.quote: Because of this archived protection template, you can't create a new label with the same name.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An encrypting default label
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against an encrypting default document label because external recipients may lack compatible apps or authorized accounts.
claims.quote: It's usually not a good idea to select a label that applies encryption as a default label to documents. ... External users who might not have apps that support the encryption or they might not use an account that can be authorized.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy scope is not an access list
claims.claim: Azure Rights Management does not support non-email-enabled security groups for label protection.
claims.quote: For labels that apply protection, Azure Rights Management doesn't support non-email-enabled security groups or exclusions

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy scope is not an access list
claims.claim: Azure Rights Management does not support publishing-policy exclusions for label protection.
claims.quote: For labels that apply protection, Azure Rights Management doesn't support non-email-enabled security groups or exclusions

claims.where: Risks and limits: A policy scope is not an access list
claims.claim: Publishing-policy scope does not necessarily determine who can access protected content.
claims.quote: The publishing policy scope doesn't necessarily determine who can access protected content.

claims.claim: A site owner can change external-sharing options by changing the site's label.
claims.quote: A site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.claim: Edits to a published label's group settings are not automatically applied to already labeled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label ... those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.
claims.fix: After this statement, add: 'Microsoft's Purview container-label guide gives different guidance: it says to wait at least 24 hours for changed site and group settings to replicate to containers that already have the label applied.' The conflicting passage is under 'Modifying published labels that are configured for sites and groups' at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites. Keep both statements attributed to their respective guides.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes take time
claims.claim: Microsoft says to allow 24 hours for label and policy changes.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes take time
claims.claim: Changes depending on group membership can take 24 to 48 hours.
claims.quote: For configurations that depend on populating a new group and group membership changes, or network replication latency and bandwidth restrictions, these changes might take 24-48 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: DLP cannot scan the contents of files uploaded directly into Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Word, Excel and PowerPoint evaluate this Copilot DLP policy at file open, so a newly applied label requires reopening the file.
claims.quote: The ... policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open. If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Label-based Copilot DLP coverage includes emails sent on or after 1 January 2025.
claims.quote: Emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Calendar invites are not supported by this label-based Copilot DLP coverage.
claims.quote: Calendar invites aren't supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Copilot DLP gaps
claims.claim: Excluded items can still appear in Copilot response citations.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices can exclude labeled content from Copilot in supported Office apps.
claims.quote: You must use the PowerShell advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices ... Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps

claims.claim: The BlockContentAnalysisServices restriction does not require the label to encrypt content.
claims.quote: You want to prevent all documents and emails with this label in Office apps from being sent to Microsoft connected experiences for analysis: ... -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.claim: That setting does not exclude the content from Copilot in Teams or Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: The content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: A tenant supports at most 500 labels applying encryption with specified users and permissions.
claims.quote: If the label applies encryption that specifies the users and permissions, there's a maximum of 500 labels per tenant supported with this configuration.

claims.claim: The documented Information Protection role groups provide Purview permissions for sensitivity-label administration.
claims.quote: You can use the following role groups: Information Protection; Information Protection Admins; Information Protection Analysts; Information Protection Investigators; Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is another supported permissions route.
claims.quote: You can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Sensitivity Label Reader supplies read-only access.
claims.quote: For a read-only role, use Sensitivity Label Reader.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are alternative administration routes.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Those label-administration permissions are not required merely to apply labels.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Assigning a label to an existing group requires group ownership or at least Groups Administrator.
claims.quote: The user must be the group owner or at least a Groups Administrator.

claims.quote: Audit sensitivity labeling in my organization | Audit log activities - Sensitivity label activities

claims.quote: You find Posture Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal: 1. Information Protection > Reports 2. Data Loss Prevention > Reports
